report:
Based on the evidence, I need to correct the premise: the current best evidence does **not** support the conclusion that ivermectin lowers COVID-19 mortality.

## What the evidence actually shows

**Early, low-quality studies suggested benefit.** Several early meta-analyses of small, often methodologically weak or fraudulent trials (2021) reported mortality reductions with ivermectin, but authors themselves rated the certainty of evidence as "low" ([springer.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S187140212100206X)). These findings drove early enthusiasm but were later undermined when high-risk-of-bias and retracted studies were excluded.

**Large, rigorous randomized trials found no benefit.** The TOGETHER trial, a well-designed placebo-controlled RCT in Brazil (NEJM, 2022), found ivermectin did not reduce hospitalization, ED visits, or other clinical outcomes compared with placebo ([nejm.org](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2115869)). A follow-up JAMA platform trial testing higher-dose ivermectin similarly found no significant improvement in outcomes ([jamanetwork.com](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2801827)).

**Updated systematic reviews (2023–2024), incorporating these larger, higher-quality trials, reversed earlier conclusions.** A 2024 systematic review/meta-analysis found ivermectin did not significantly improve mortality, ICU admission, or ventilator use, though it may modestly ease symptoms ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38510038](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38510038/)).

**Regulatory and guideline bodies concur.** The FDA states available trial data do not demonstrate ivermectin is effective against COVID-19, and in November 2023 the WHO strongly recommended *against* using ivermectin to treat COVID-19, citing lack of evidence ([en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivermectin_during_the_COVID-19_pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivermectin_during_the_COVID-19_pandemic)).

## Bottom line
The scientific consensus, based on the largest and most rigorous randomized trials, is that ivermectin does **not** reduce COVID-19 mortality. Earlier claims of benefit came from smaller, lower-quality, or since-discredited studies. Major health authorities (WHO, FDA) now recommend against its use for COVID-19.
